the dipolar phase relaxation enhancement is sensitive to changes in the average position of the FeS domain and that the average equilibrium FeS position can be changed by mutations and inhibitors of cytochrome b.
the FeS cluster in cytochrome bc is in a dynamic distribution of positions, and the distribution is modifiable by chemical modifications.
the dipolar enhancement of the FeS phase relaxation in cytochrome bc is sensitive to changes in the FeS position in the catalytic core, and that the FeS position is modifiable.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to study large-scale motions of the catalytic subunits in the bc1 complex, which is a key enzyme in biological energy conversion.
the development of a new spectroscopic parameter which can be used to study the movement of a large-scale structural domain in proteins.
the development of a new method of studying large-scale movements of protein domains by means of magnetic interactions between cofactors of the protein redox chains.

the dipolar enhancement of the phase relaxation is a sensitive probe of the FeS position and its changes.
the dipolar enhancement of the FeS phase relaxation in cytochrome bc 1 provides a sensitive and specific spectroscopic parameter for the measurement of the distance between the FeS head and heme b L.
the dipolar enhancement of the phase relaxation of the iron−sulphur cluster is a sensitive parameter that can be used to study the movement of the iron− sulphur head domain of cytochrome bcl.

the dipolar relaxation enhancement is sensitive to the distance between heme bL and FeS, which in turn is sensitive to the orienting potential of the protein.

magnetic interactions can be used as a spectroscopic tool to sense changes in the distance of a pair of redox cofactors in a protein.
